svg.title: A fictional requirement-to-release trace retains the overwrite rationale
svg.desc: Purpose links connect IMP42 and D7 to preview C1 and confirmation C2. Only the horizontal C1-to-C2 arrow means parent-to-child ancestry. Other connectors name assessment, integration and release identity relationships. All history labels are fictional.
svg.text: Trace an overwrite to its accepted decision
All history IDs are fictional · no review, merge or release executed
IMP42 / D7 · revised acceptance
Listed SKUs replace quantities; absent SKUs remain unchanged.
D7 explicitly supersedes the earlier create-only policy.
Purpose links: preview and confirmation implement the revised outcome
C1 · preview + T1
P100:99 → replace
P201:3 → create
T1: no inventory writes
C2 · confirmation + T2
D7: replace listed stock
P900 stays 8.
C1 → C2: parent-to-child ancestry; T1/T2 identify their source version
R2 · assessed range H0..C2
T1 and T2 at C2 support the review; approval is not integration.
Map the reviewed head to the integrated version
M2 · integration record
Parents H0 and C2; I2 records separate integration evidence.
Release record identifies source, artifact and configuration
REL7 · source M2 · artifact A7 · configuration CFG2
Real records retain resolvable revisions and built-byte digests.
This fictional mapping does not establish deployed or running state.
Each connector means its written relation; this is not one commit graph.
